name: HITT Contracting
hq: Falls Church, VA, USA (new 270,000 sq ft net-zero HQ delivering early 2027)
founded: 1937 (Warren & Myrtle Hitt, as W.A. HITT Decorating Co., Arlington VA; renamed HITT Contracting 1989)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: HITT is America's #1-ranked data-center builder by revenue (ENR 2025 telecom/data-center list; listed first on BD+C's 2025 ranking) — a family-owned Falls Church, VA contractor that converted a high-velocity DC-metro interiors business into the fastest-compounding mission-critical franchise in the industry. Revenue ran $5.6B (2023) → $8.7B (2024, first ENR top-10) → $13.0B (2025, ENR #8), with ENR survey data attributing 82% of 2025 revenue to the data-center category, delivered 100% CM-at-risk. The franchise is anchored inside Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley (the world's largest market: 4,900 MW built, 5,500 MW planned) with QTS (7M+ sq ft delivered together), Vantage, Corscale, Microsoft (48 MW Alviso campus, groundbroke June 2026), and federal/GSA work; its calling card is speed — a 22.5 MW facility in a record 180 days (Sterling II), a 250,000 sq ft Vantage building pad-to-ribbon in seven months. Two 2025-26 acquisitions (Central Consulting — tri-state healthcare; Brycon — Intel/Samsung cleanroom builder) extend the book into healthcare and semiconductors. Watch items: a ~$24M uninsured layer from the $51M Glenstone settlement (Virginia Court of Appeals affirmed the insurer's late-notice denial 2026-08-04), an April 2025 fatal trench collapse at the Vantage Ashburn campus still without a published citation outcome, and 82% single-sector concentration. Collection gap: fully private — no margins, backlog, or balance-sheet disclosure; revenue is self-reported to rankers.
ecosystemRole: The AI buildout's speed specialist: the #1 US data-center GC by revenue, converting hyperscaler and colocation capex into commissioned megawatts faster than any ranked peer, from a home base inside the world's largest data-center market.

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess HITT's #1 data-center-revenue position rests on a speed franchise inherited from its interiors DNA — thousands of fast, small, repeat-client jobs bred a velocity culture (180-day 22.5 MW delivery; 7-month pad-to-ribbon) that translates directly into the metric hyperscalers and colos now pay a premium for: time-to-commissioned-megawatts. Peers with heavy-civil lineages cannot easily copy a culture built on $2M fit-outs.

2. (High confidence) We assess sector concentration is the defining risk: 82% of 2025 revenue in one category, delivered 100% CM-at-risk, in a market (NoVA) facing land costs +45% YoY, grid constraints, and rising public resistance. The Central Consulting and Brycon acquisitions are read as deliberate concentration hedges — healthcare and semiconductors are the two adjacent capex pools that use the same technical-construction muscle.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the home-market advantage is still widening: NoVA holds 4,900 MW built with >90% of inventory pre-committed through 2026-27 and 5,500 MW planned, and HITT is investing directly in the constraint (the NOVA community-college trades center) rather than only competing for scarce labor. As long as Data Center Alley absorbs capacity this fast, the #1 slot is HITT's to lose in its own backyard.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the Glenstone episode (settling at $51M after rejecting an ~$11M mediation package, then losing a ~$24M insurance layer on late notice, affirmed on appeal 2026-08-04) as an isolated legacy-project failure rather than a systemic quality signal — it predates the data-center scale-up — but it is a real one-time capital hit for a private balance sheet and a governance lesson on claims discipline.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess the two-owner family structure (Brett Hitt and Jim Millar as co-chairmen, professional management under CEO Kim Roy since 2017) is a competitive asset in this cycle: it funds long-horizon bets — Co|Lab, the net-zero HQ, an R&D program in an industry that spends <1% of revenue on R&D — that build exactly the sustainability brand hyperscaler clients screen for. The cost is opacity: no margin, backlog, or debt disclosure exists to verify how profitably the $13B is being built.

6. (Low confidence) We assess HITT's implied data-center revenue (~$10.7B at the ENR 82% mix) may overstate durable run-rate — the figure is survey-derived, unaudited, and one hyperscaler pause in NoVA would compress it quickly. Treat the mix precision as indicative.
